treats.title: Peanut Butter Pumpkin Biscuits
treats.subtitle: crunchy bone-shaped biscuits — the classic good-pup cookie
treats.dogSafe: Pure pumpkin is gentle on tummies and peanut butter is safe when it's xylitol-free. No salt or sugar added.

items.name: whole wheat flour
items.note: or oat flour for sensitive pups

items.name: pure pumpkin purée
items.note: NOT pumpkin pie filling (it has spices + sugar)
items.warn: Pie filling has nutmeg and sugar — use 100% pure pumpkin.

items.name: natural peanut butter
items.warn: Check the label: NO xylitol (also called birch sugar). Plain, unsalted is best.

items.name: water
items.note: only if the dough is dry

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment.

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.text: Stir the flour, pumpkin, eggs and peanut butter together until it forms a stiff dough. Add water 1 tbsp at a time only if it's too dry to hold together.

steps.title: Roll and cut
steps.text: Roll out on a floured counter to about 1 cm (½ in) thick. Cut into bones (or squares with a knife) and lay them on the sheet — they don't spread.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 20 minutes, flip, then bake 15–20 minutes more until firm and golden.

steps.title: Dry out for crunch
steps.text: Turn the oven off and leave the biscuits inside with the door cracked for 1 hour. Drier biscuits keep longer.

steps.title: Cool completely
steps.text: Cool on a rack before sharing or storing. Good pup!

treats.storage: Airtight jar at room temp 1 week, fridge 3 weeks, freezer 3 months.
tips: Bake them extra-dry if you want them to last longer on the counter.
Small dog? Use a tiny cutter — calories add up fast.
treats.source: Adapted from the American Kennel Club (AKC) pumpkin peanut butter dog treat recipe; ingredient safety per ASPCA Animal Poison Control.

basic.note: Three ingredients: flour, pumpkin and egg.

stepNotes.1: Basic: no peanut butter — add a spoon more pumpkin.

fancy.note: Two-tone biscuits with a plain yogurt drizzle and blueberries pressed in.

items.name: plain unsweetened yogurt
items.warn: Plain, unsweetened, no xylitol.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Press a blueberry into each bone before baking. Once completely cool, drizzle thin lines of plain yogurt and let them set in the fridge. Keep the drizzled ones in the fridge.

why.0-1: Pumpkin binds the dough and is gentle on tummies.

treats.funFact: Plain pumpkin is rich in soluble fibre, which is why vets often suggest a spoonful to help keep a dog’s digestion on track, in either direction.

treats.title: Frozen Yogurt Pupsicles
treats.subtitle: cool, creamy paw-shaped bites of yogurt, banana and peanut butter
treats.dogSafe: Plain yogurt and banana are dog-safe in small amounts. Pick yogurt with no sweeteners — some 'light' yogurts contain xylitol.

items.name: plain unsweetened yogurt
items.warn: Plain only — no xylitol, no artificial sweeteners, no flavours.

items.name: natural peanut butter
items.warn: Check the label: NO xylitol (also called birch sugar). Plain, unsalted is best.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Mash or blend the yogurt, banana and peanut butter until smooth.

steps.title: Fill the moulds
steps.text: Spoon into a silicone paw or ice-cube mould and tap it on the counter to settle.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Freeze at least 4 hours, until solid. Pop out and store in a freezer bag.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Give one at a time, outside or on a towel. New to dairy? Start with half a pupsicle to check Acura's tummy.

tips: Some dogs are lactose-sensitive — start small.
Swap the yogurt for pure pumpkin purée for a dairy-free version.
treats.source: Based on AKC and PetMD frozen yogurt dog treat guidance (plain, unsweetened yogurt; xylitol-free peanut butter).

fancy.note: Layered pupsicles with blueberries and strawberries.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: drop berries into each mould before filling.

why.0-0: Yogurt makes them creamy — start small if Acura is new to dairy.

treats.funFact: Many adult dogs make less lactase, the enzyme that digests milk sugar. Plain yogurt is gentler than milk because its live cultures have already broken down much of the lactose.

treats.title: Sweet Potato Chews
treats.subtitle: slow-baked, chewy single-ingredient strips
treats.dogSafe: Plain cooked sweet potato is a healthy, fibre-rich treat. Never season it — no butter, salt, onion or garlic.

steps.title: Heat the oven low
steps.text: Heat the oven to 120°C (250°F) and line 2 baking sheets with parchment.

steps.title: Slice
steps.text: Cut the sweet potatoes lengthwise into 6 mm (¼ in) slices, then into strips. Even thickness = even drying.

steps.title: Bake low and slow
steps.text: Lay in a single layer and bake 1½ hours, then flip.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Bake 1–1½ hours more until dry and leathery (chewy) or crisp at the edges. Thinner strips finish sooner.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool completely on the sheets — they firm up as they cool.

treats.storage: Fridge in an airtight container up to 3 weeks, or freeze up to 3 months.
tips: Chewy strips are softer on older teeth; crisp ones last longer.
Supervise chewing and cut into smaller pieces for gulpers.
treats.source: Based on AKC 'sweet potato chews' guidance and PetMD notes on sweet potato for dogs (plain, cooked, unseasoned).

basic.note: Already as simple as it gets: one sweet potato, low and slow.

fancy.note: Mixed sweet potato and apple chews.

items.name: apple
items.warn: No seeds or core.

stepNotes.2: Fancy: add apple rings to the tray — they finish about 30 minutes sooner.

why.0-0: Even slices dry evenly — thickness matters more than anything else.

treats.funFact: Sweet potatoes are orange from beta-carotene. Unlike cats, dogs can turn beta-carotene into vitamin A, which helps their eyes, skin and coat.

treats.title: Banana Oat Bites
treats.subtitle: soft, chewy 3-ingredient bites — great training rewards
treats.dogSafe: Oats and banana are dog-safe in moderation. Use plain rolled oats — never instant flavoured packets (they can have raisins or chocolate).

items.name: plain rolled oats
items.warn: Plain oats only — no flavoured or raisin packets.

items.name: natural peanut butter
items.warn: Check the label: NO xylitol (also called birch sugar). Plain, unsalted is best.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Mash the bananas, then stir in the oats, egg and peanut butter until it's a sticky dough. Let it sit 5 minutes so the oats soak.

steps.title: Scoop
steps.text: Roll tablespoons into balls, set on the sheet and press each with a fork.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 15–18 minutes until set and golden on the bottom.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool completely. Break in half for small rewards.

treats.storage: Fridge in an airtight container up to 1 week; freezer up to 3 months.
tips: Soft treats are great for training — break them into pea-size pieces.
treats.source: Adapted from AKC and Rover vet-reviewed banana oat dog treat recipes.

fancy.note: With blueberries and a yogurt dip.

items.name: plain unsweetened yogurt
items.warn: Plain, unsweetened, no xylitol.

stepNotes.4: Fancy: dip the cooled tops in yogurt and chill to set.

why.0-0: Ripe banana sweetens and binds — no sugar needed.
why.0-1: Oats give structure; plain rolled oats only.

treats.funFact: Bananas are a sweet, potassium-rich snack for dogs, but they’re high in sugar, so vets suggest only a few slices at a time.

treats.title: Plain Chicken Jerky
treats.subtitle: one-ingredient chewy strips — high-value treat time
treats.dogSafe: Plain chicken is dog-safe. Never season it (no salt, garlic or onion) and heat it to 74°C (165°F) first so it's food-safe.

items.name: boneless skinless chicken breasts
items.note: about 600 g, partly frozen for slicing

steps.title: Slice thin
steps.text: Freeze the chicken 30 minutes, then slice with the grain into strips about 3–5 mm thick. Trim any fat.

steps.title: Make it food-safe
steps.text: Lay the strips on a parchment-lined sheet and bake at 160°C (325°F) for 10 minutes so they reach 74°C (165°F) — the USDA-recommended step before drying.

steps.title: Dry low and slow
steps.text: Lower the oven to 95°C (200°F) and bake 2–2½ hours, flipping halfway, until completely dry and they snap or bend without any moisture.

steps.title: Cool and store
steps.text: Cool completely, then store in the fridge. Wash hands, boards and counters well — raw chicken can carry salmonella.

treats.storage: Fridge in an airtight container up to 2 weeks; freezer up to 3 months.
tips: Completely dry = longer life. Any bendy, moist spots? Dry 20–30 minutes more.
Break into small pieces for training.
treats.source: Method follows USDA guidance for drying meat (heat to 74°C / 165°F before dehydrating); dog-safety per AKC homemade chicken jerky notes.

basic.note: Plain chicken, nothing else — the classic.

fancy.note: Chicken and sweet potato wraps.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: wrap a thin chicken strip around each sweet potato stick before baking.

why.0-0: Trimming all the fat keeps the jerky safe to store and gentle on tummies.

treats.funFact: Dogs have about 1,700 taste buds to our roughly 9,000, but theirs are tuned to meat, and they even have taste buds that respond to water.

treats.title: Apple Carrot Bites
treats.subtitle: crunchy little biscuits with grated apple and carrot
treats.dogSafe: Apple (without seeds or core) and carrot are dog-safe crunchy foods. Always remove apple seeds and the core.

items.name: apple
items.warn: Remove the core and every seed — apple seeds aren't safe for dogs.

items.name: oat flour
items.note: blitz rolled oats in a blender

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Stir the grated apple, carrot and egg, then mix in the oat flour. Add water a spoonful at a time until it holds together.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Roll to 1 cm thick and cut small bones, or roll teaspoon-size balls and flatten with a fork.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 22–25 minutes until firm and lightly golden.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool completely on a rack.

treats.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; freezer up to 3 months.
tips: Grate the apple and carrot finely so the bites hold together.
treats.source: Adapted from AKC and PetMD apple and carrot dog treat guidance (core and seeds removed).

basic.note: Already basic: apple, carrot, egg and oat flour — nothing to leave out.

fancy.note: With a little pumpkin and blueberries.

items.name: pure pumpkin purée
items.warn: 100% pure pumpkin, not pie filling.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: stir in the pumpkin and blueberries.

why.0-0: Apple adds sweetness and moisture — always core it and remove the seeds.

treats.funFact: Apple is a great crunchy snack for dogs, but the core and seeds always come out: apple seeds contain amygdalin, which releases cyanide when chewed.

treats.title: Turkey & Sweet Potato Training Bites
treats.subtitle: soft little squares for training — easy to break, easy to love
treats.dogSafe: Plain cooked turkey and sweet potato are both dog-safe. No salt, onion or garlic, and the turkey is baked to 74°C (165°F).

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and line a 23×33 cm (9×13 in) pan with parchment.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Mix the turkey, sweet potato, egg and oat flour with your hands until even.

steps.title: Spread
steps.text: Press it into the pan in an even layer about 1 cm thick.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 25–30 minutes, until firm, lightly golden and 74°C (165°F) in the centre.

steps.title: Cool and cut
steps.text: Cool in the pan, lift out on the parchment and cut into 1.5 cm squares. Wash hands, boards and counters after the raw turkey.

treats.storage: Fridge in an airtight container 4 days; freezer bag 3 months (thaw a handful at a time).
tips: Freeze in small bags so only a few days' worth is thawed.
Cut smaller for a puppy class: 1 cm squares are about 6 kcal.
treats.source: Ground poultry cooked to 74°C (165°F) per Health Canada; dog-safety per AKC and ASPCA Animal Poison Control.

basic.note: Turkey, egg and oat flour only.

stepNotes.1: Basic: no sweet potato; add 2 tbsp water if it's crumbly.

fancy.note: Carrot and peas folded through for colour.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: mix in the carrot and peas too.

why.0-1: Sweet potato keeps the bites soft and adds fibre.
why.0-2: The egg binds it so the squares hold together.

treats.funFact: Food rewards work best in tiny pieces: trainers aim for a bite a dog can swallow in a second so the lesson keeps moving.

treats.title: Cheesy Carrot Crunchers
treats.subtitle: crunchy biscuits with a little cheddar and carrot
treats.dogSafe: Carrots are dog-safe and a little mild cheddar is fine for most dogs. Skip the cheese if Acura's tummy is sensitive to dairy.

items.name: shredded mild cheddar
items.note: a little goes a long way

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment.

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.text: Stir the flour, carrot, cheddar and egg together, then add the water a little at a time until it holds as a firm dough.

steps.title: Roll and cut
steps.text: Roll out on a floured counter about 1 cm thick and cut into bones or squares. Set them on the sheet; they don't spread.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 25–30 minutes, flipping halfway, until firm and golden at the edges.

steps.title: Dry out for crunch
steps.text: Turn the oven off and leave them inside with the door cracked for 1 hour.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool completely on a rack before storing.

treats.storage: Airtight jar 1 week; fridge 2 weeks; freezer 3 months.
tips: Grate the carrot finely so the dough rolls smoothly.
Small cutter = fewer calories per treat.
treats.source: Adapted from AKC homemade biscuit guidance; ingredient safety per ASPCA Animal Poison Control.

fancy.note: A pinch of cheddar melted on top of each one.

stepNotes.3: Fancy: sprinkle the extra cheddar over the tops before baking.

why.0-2: Cheese makes them smell irresistible; a little is plenty.

treats.funFact: A dog's nose has up to 300 million scent receptors to our roughly 6 million, so a little cheddar smells like a lot.

treats.title: Blueberry Oat Crunchers
treats.subtitle: purple-speckled oat biscuits with pumpkin
treats.dogSafe: Blueberries, oats and plain pumpkin are all dog-safe. Wheat-free for pups who do better without it.

items.name: pure pumpkin purée
items.warn: Use 100% pure pumpkin, not pie filling (it is spiced and sweetened).

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment.

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.text: Stir the oat flour, blueberries, pumpkin and egg into a soft dough. Add a spoon more oat flour if it's sticky.

steps.title: Roll and cut
steps.text: Roll out between two sheets of parchment about 1 cm thick and cut into small shapes.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 22–25 minutes until firm and dry on top.

steps.title: Dry out for crunch
steps.text: Turn the oven off and leave them inside with the door cracked for 1 hour.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool completely on a rack.

treats.storage: Airtight jar 1 week; fridge 2 weeks; freezer 3 months.
tips: Oat dough is stickier than wheat; parchment on top makes rolling easy.
Frozen wild blueberries are cheapest and work well.
treats.source: Ingredient safety per ASPCA Animal Poison Control and AKC 'Can dogs eat blueberries?'.

fancy.note: A thin drizzle of plain yogurt on top.

items.name: plain unsweetened yogurt
items.warn: Plain, unsweetened, no xylitol.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Once completely cool, drizzle thin lines of yogurt over them and let them set in the fridge. Keep the drizzled ones in the fridge.

why.0-2: Pumpkin binds the oat dough and is gentle on tummies.

treats.funFact: Blueberries get their deep colour from anthocyanins, the same family of pigments that makes red cabbage purple.

treats.title: Frozen Watermelon Bites
treats.subtitle: one-ingredient summer cool-downs
treats.dogSafe: Watermelon flesh is dog-safe and mostly water. Remove all seeds and the rind, which can upset tummies.

items.name: seedless watermelon
items.note: cut in 1.5 cm cubes, rind and any seeds removed

steps.title: Prep
steps.text: Cut the flesh off the rind and pick out any seeds. Cut into 1.5 cm cubes.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Spread the cubes on a parchment-lined tray, not touching, and freeze 2 hours until firm.

steps.title: Store
steps.text: Tip into a freezer bag.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Give a few at a time outside on a hot day. Let a very cold cube sit a minute for a small dog.

tips: Watermelon is about 92% water, a nice way to help her drink on hot days.
Big dog? Give larger chunks so she chews instead of gulping.
treats.source: AKC 'Can dogs eat watermelon?'; ASPCA Animal Poison Control.

fancy.note: Watermelon and yogurt swirl paws.

items.name: plain unsweetened yogurt
items.warn: Plain, unsweetened, no xylitol.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: blend half the cubes smooth, swirl with the yogurt in a silicone paw mould and freeze 4 hours with the cubes.

why.0-0: Seeds and rind come off: the rind is tough to digest and seeds can cause a blockage.

treats.funFact: Watermelon is a berry botanically, and it's about 92% water.

treats.title: Salmon & Sweet Potato Bites
treats.subtitle: soft fishy bites she'll do anything for
treats.dogSafe: Plain cooked salmon is dog-safe. Cook it through (never raw), remove every bone and skip seasoning.

steps.title: Cook the salmon
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Bake the salmon on a parchment-lined sheet 12–15 minutes, until it flakes and reads 70°C (158°F). Cool, flake and pick out any bones.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Lower the oven to 175°C (350°F). Mash the salmon, sweet potato, egg and oat flour together.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Roll into 2 cm balls, set them on the sheet and press each flat with a fork.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 18–20 minutes, until firm and 74°C (165°F) in the centre.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool completely on a rack.

tips: Run your fingers through the flaked salmon twice; pin bones hide.
Leftover plain salmon from dinner works if it had no glaze or garlic.
treats.source: Fish cooked to 70°C (158°F) per Health Canada; dog-safety per AKC 'Can dogs eat salmon?'.

basic.note: Plain salmon, sweet potato, egg and oats, as written.

fancy.note: Peas folded in.

why.0-0: Salmon brings omega-3 fats dogs love the smell of.
why.0-2: The egg binds the bites so they hold.

treats.funFact: Salmon is rich in omega-3 fats, which is why so many dog foods and coat supplements use fish oil.

treats.title: Dried Apple Rings
treats.subtitle: chewy single-ingredient rings, seeds gone
treats.dogSafe: Apple flesh is dog-safe. The core and seeds always come out.

items.name: Gala apples
items.warn: Apple seeds and cores are on the never list.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 95°C (200°F) and line two baking sheets with parchment.

steps.title: Slice
steps.text: Core the apples with a corer and check each slice for seeds. Slice 3 mm thick and lay them flat, not touching.

steps.title: Dry low and slow
steps.text: Bake 2–2½ hours, flipping halfway, until leathery and dry with no wet spots.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool on the sheets; they firm up as they cool.

tips: A mandoline makes even slices so they dry at the same rate.
Break a ring in pieces for a small dog.
treats.source: AKC 'Can dogs eat apples?'; ASPCA Animal Poison Control (apple seeds and cores).

fancy.note: Peanut butter sandwich rings at serving.

items.name: natural peanut butter
items.warn: Check the label: NO xylitol (also called birch sugar). Plain, unsalted is best.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: To serve, spread a thin layer of peanut butter between two rings. Make them just before giving.

why.0-0: Gala is naturally sweet, so nothing else is needed.

treats.funFact: Apple seeds contain amygdalin, which releases cyanide when crushed, which is why the core always comes out.

treats.title: Birthday Pupcakes
treats.subtitle: mini pumpkin-peanut cakes with yogurt frosting
treats.dogSafe: Every ingredient is dog-safe: xylitol-free peanut butter, plain pumpkin, carrot and plain yogurt. No icing, sprinkles or chocolate.

items.name: natural peanut butter
items.warn: Check the label: NO xylitol (also called birch sugar). Plain, unsalted is best.

items.name: pure pumpkin purée
items.warn: Use 100% pure pumpkin, not pie filling (it is spiced and sweetened).

items.name: plain unsweetened Greek yogurt
items.warn: Plain, unsweetened, no xylitol.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a 24-cup mini muffin tin.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Whisk the flour and baking powder. In another bowl stir the egg, peanut butter, pumpkin, carrot, oil and water, then fold in the flour until just mixed.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Fill the cups two-thirds full and bake 15–18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool 10 minutes in the tin, then completely on a rack.

steps.title: Frost
steps.text: Spread or pipe a little yogurt on each just before the party. Keep frosted ones in the fridge.

treats.storage: Unfrosted: fridge 4 days, freezer 2 months. Frosted: fridge 2 days.
tips: One mini pupcake is a big treat for a small dog; halve it.
Freeze extras unfrosted for next time.
treats.source: Adapted from AKC dog birthday cake guidance; ingredient safety per ASPCA Animal Poison Control.

fancy.note: A blueberry crown on each one.

stepNotes.4: Fancy: press a few blueberries into the frosting.

why.0-1: Baking powder makes them light and cake-like.
why.0-4: Pumpkin keeps them moist without anything sweet added.

treats.funFact: Dogs can taste sweetness, but much more weakly than we do; the peanut butter smell is what gets the party going.

treats.title: Beef Liver Training Bites
treats.subtitle: the jackpot treat for recall practice
treats.dogSafe: Cooked liver is dog-safe in small amounts. It's very rich in vitamin A, so keep it to a few bites a day.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and line a 20×20 cm (8 in) pan with parchment.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Blend the liver smooth in a blender or food processor, then add the egg and oat flour and pulse to a thick batter.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Spread it 1 cm thick in the pan and bake 20–25 minutes, until firm, springy and 74°C (165°F) in the centre.

steps.title: Cool and cut
steps.text: Cool, lift out and cut into 1 cm cubes. Wash the blender, hands and counters well after raw liver.

tips: Liver is very rich in vitamin A: a few cubes a day, not handfuls.
Freeze most of the batch in small bags for training weeks.
treats.source: Dog-safety and vitamin A caution per AKC 'Can dogs eat liver?'; cooked to 74°C (165°F) per Health Canada for organ meats and egg dishes.

basic.note: Liver, egg and oats, as written.

fancy.note: Softer pumpkin-liver bites.

items.name: pure pumpkin purée
items.warn: Use 100% pure pumpkin, not pie filling (it is spiced and sweetened).

stepNotes.1: Fancy: blend in the pumpkin with the egg.

why.0-0: Liver is the strongest-smelling, highest-value reward for hard lessons.

treats.funFact: Liver is the body's vitamin A store: 100 g of beef liver has several days' worth for a medium dog, which is why it's a treat, not a meal.

treats.title: Green Bean Crisps
treats.subtitle: light, crunchy, nearly calorie-free
treats.dogSafe: Plain green beans are dog-safe and low in calories. No oil or salt.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 120°C (250°F) and line two baking sheets with parchment.

steps.title: Blanch
steps.text: Boil the beans 3 minutes, drain and pat completely dry.

steps.title: Dry
steps.text: Spread them on the sheets, not touching, and bake 1½–2 hours, shaking the pans every 30 minutes, until crisp and snapping.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool on the sheets; any bendy ones go back in for 15 minutes.

tips: A good swap when she's watching her weight.
Store with a paper towel in the jar to keep them crisp.
treats.source: AKC 'Can dogs eat green beans?'.

fancy.note: A mix of green beans and carrot coins.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: blanch the carrot coins with the beans.

why.0-0: Blanching first sets the colour and helps them dry evenly.

treats.funFact: Vets often suggest green beans as a low-calorie filler for dogs that need to slim down.

treats.title: Chicken Broth Ice Cubes
treats.subtitle: homemade no-salt broth frozen with chicken bits
treats.dogSafe: Made from plain chicken and water. Never use store-bought broth: most are seasoned and very salty.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Simmer the chicken in the water, partly covered, 20–25 minutes, until 74°C (165°F) in the thickest part.

steps.title: Cool and skim
steps.text: Lift out the chicken. Cool the broth, then chill it and lift off the fat.

steps.title: Fill the trays
steps.text: Chop a little of the chicken very small and drop a few bits into each ice-cube cup. Pour the broth over.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Freeze at least 4 hours, until solid, then pop into a freezer bag. Keep the rest of the plain chicken for her dinners this week.

tips: Skimming the fat keeps them gentle on her tummy.
Pop one in her water bowl on a hot day.
treats.source: Poultry cooked to 74°C (165°F) per Health Canada; ASPCA Animal Poison Control on seasoned foods.

basic.note: Plain broth cubes, no chicken bits.

fancy.note: Peas and carrot frozen in with the chicken.

stepNotes.0: Fancy: add the carrot and peas for the last 5 minutes.
stepNotes.2: Fancy: spoon a little carrot and peas into each cup too.

why.0-0: Thighs give a richer broth; trim the fat so it's light.

treats.funFact: Dogs cool off mostly by panting; the only places they really sweat are their paw pads.

treats.title: Frozen Kibble & Pumpkin Stuffer
treats.subtitle: a long-lasting lick-and-chew puzzle for a chew toy
treats.kcal: ~20 kcal per toy plus the kibble (count it in her meal)
treats.dogSafe: Her own kibble plus plain pumpkin and plain yogurt. Count the kibble as part of her daily food.

items.name: pure pumpkin purée
items.warn: Use 100% pure pumpkin, not pie filling (it is spiced and sweetened).

items.name: plain unsweetened yogurt
items.warn: Plain, unsweetened, no xylitol.

steps.title: Soften
steps.text: Soak the kibble in warm water 10 minutes until soft, then drain.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Mash the kibble with the pumpkin and yogurt.

steps.title: Stuff
steps.text: Pack it into two hollow rubber chew toys, pressing it in firmly.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Stand the toys upright in a mug and freeze at least 4 hours.

tips: Frozen toys take longer: great for when we leave the house.
Wash the toys well between uses.
treats.source: Enrichment guidance per AKC; ingredient safety per ASPCA Animal Poison Control.

fancy.note: Layered with blueberries.

stepNotes.2: Fancy: drop a few blueberries in between the layers.

why.0-0: Using her own kibble keeps the calories in her normal day.

treats.funFact: Licking and chewing release calming endorphins in dogs, which is why trainers use frozen toys for alone time.

treats.title: No-Bake Peanut Butter Oat Balls
treats.subtitle: five-minute rolled bites from the fridge
treats.dogSafe: Rolled oats, plain pumpkin and xylitol-free peanut butter are all dog-safe.

items.name: natural peanut butter
items.warn: Check the label: NO xylitol (also called birch sugar). Plain, unsalted is best.

items.name: pure pumpkin purée
items.warn: Use 100% pure pumpkin, not pie filling (it is spiced and sweetened).

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Stir the oats, peanut butter, pumpkin and flaxseed into a stiff mix. Add a spoon of oats if it's sticky.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: Roll into 1.5 cm balls and set them on a parchment-lined plate.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Chill 30 minutes until firm.

tips: Damp hands stop the mix sticking.
Quick oats roll smoother than large flakes.
treats.source: Ingredient safety per ASPCA Animal Poison Control; AKC 'Can dogs eat oatmeal?'.

fancy.note: A blueberry pressed into each.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: press a blueberry into each ball.

why.0-3: Flax adds omega-3 fats for a shiny coat.

treats.funFact: Oats are one of the few grains naturally rich in soluble fibre called beta-glucan.

treats.title: Christmas Cranberry Oat Stars
treats.subtitle: crunchy holiday stars for her stocking
treats.dogSafe: Fresh cranberries are dog-safe in small amounts. Never use dried cranberry mixes; they can hide other dried fruit and sweeteners.

items.name: pure pumpkin purée
items.warn: Use 100% pure pumpkin, not pie filling (it is spiced and sweetened).

items.name: fresh or frozen cranberries
items.warn: Fresh or frozen only: dried mixes can hide other dried fruit.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment.

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.text: Stir the flour, oats, pumpkin, egg and cranberries together, adding the water a little at a time until it holds.

steps.title: Roll and cut
steps.text: Roll out on a floured counter about 1 cm thick and cut into stars.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 25–30 minutes, flipping halfway, until firm and golden.

steps.title: Dry out for crunch
steps.text: Turn the oven off and leave them inside with the door cracked for 1 hour.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool completely on a rack.

tips: Tie a few in a cellophane bag with ribbon for her stocking.
Make them small: she'll get more of them.
treats.source: AKC 'Can dogs eat cranberries?'; ASPCA Animal Poison Control.

fancy.note: Half-dipped in plain Greek yogurt.

items.name: plain unsweetened Greek yogurt
items.warn: Plain, unsweetened, no xylitol.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Dip one point of each cooled star in the yogurt, set on parchment and freeze 1 hour to set. Keep the dipped ones in the freezer.

why.0-4: Chopped fresh cranberries give red flecks without anything sweet.

treats.funFact: Ripe cranberries bounce: growers have sorted them for over a century by dropping them past bounce boards.

treats.title: Pumpkin Pup Pancakes
treats.subtitle: silver-dollar weekend pancakes, plain for her
treats.dogSafe: Plain flour, pumpkin and egg cooked through. No butter, syrup or toppings from our plates.

items.name: pure pumpkin purée
items.warn: Use 100% pure pumpkin, not pie filling (it is spiced and sweetened).

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Whisk the flour, pumpkin, egg and water into a thick batter.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Heat a nonstick skillet over medium-low with no butter or oil. Drop teaspoons of batter and cook 2 minutes a side until set all the way through, in batches.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool on a rack, then break into pieces for training or give whole.

tips: Make hers while ours cook; use a separate pan with nothing in it.
Freeze flat, then bag.
treats.source: Ingredient safety per ASPCA Animal Poison Control and AKC.

fancy.note: Blueberries in the batter and a dab of yogurt on top.

items.name: plain unsweetened yogurt
items.warn: Plain, unsweetened, no xylitol.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: press a blueberry or two into each one as it cooks.
stepNotes.2: Fancy: add a tiny dab of yogurt just before serving.

why.0-2: The egg makes them hold together; cook until no wet batter shows.
